INDIAN YOUNG LAWYERS ASSOCIATION VERSUS THE STATE OF KERALA#

[Indian Young Lawyers Association versus the State of Kerala] is a 2018 case related to the entry of women aged between 10 and 50 into the Sabrimala Temple in Kerala. [Indira Gandhi versus Raj Narain] is one of the most, if not the most, momentous cases in post-independent Indian history, which brought a plethora of changes in Indian politics as well as society. item.title: Maneka Gandhi vs The Union of India
item.description:
MANEKA GANDHI VS. THE UNION OF INDIA#

[Maneka Gandhi versus the Union of India] is a landmark case that provided a new interpretation of fundamental rights. The case dates back to 1978. Maneka Gandhi, on receiving a notice from the Regional Passport Officer to surrender her passport and not finding any legitimate reason to do so, filed a writ petition under Article 32. She argued that the notice violates her right of Personal Liberty accorded in Article 21 of the Indian Constitution. A bench of 7 judges was formed for the hearing of the petition.

item.title: SC Landmark Judgments Research
item.description:
“The foremost task of the Supreme Court is to interpret the Constitution which is but a means of ordering the life of a progressive people.” - The First Attorney General of India, M.C Setalvad.

Upholding the sanctity of the Constitution: Basic Structure Doctrine

  1. Shankari Prasad Singh Deo v. Union of India (1951)

Shankari Prasad, a West Bengal zamindar, challenged the First Amendment Act, 1951, which curtailed the right to property to facilitate the abolition of zamindari and land redistribution. The Supreme Court held that constitutional amendments are not "laws" under Article 13(2), meaning amendments fall outside the restriction on laws protecting fundamental rights. This gave Parliament unlimited power to amend any provision, including fundamental rights. This case removed legal barriers to agrarian reforms and set the precedent for absolute parliamentary amendment power.​
